nodes.label: drive_sync.py — the recommended sync route
nodes.rationale: Talks to Drive v3 directly, streams every download in 8 MiB chunks to a temp file and moves it atomically, so nothing is held whole in memory and there is no size ceiling.

nodes.label: The Claude Drive connector's payload ceiling
nodes.rationale: Bisected on 2026-09-02 between 6,303,034 B succeeding and 6,365,840 B failing; the oversized response tears the MCP session down. Re-measured 2026-09-04 as an explicit 10 MB refusal instead.

nodes.label: The governing constraint is context, not the size limit
nodes.rationale: Everything the connector returns is spent as model context at 4 base64 chars per 3 bytes; one 388 MB export costs 129-148M tokens against a 15M session budget, and chunking does not change a total. The dividing line is whether bytes pass through context or go straight to disk.

nodes.label: --adopt — recording a file this tool did not download
nodes.rationale: A same-titled duplicate is invisible to a mount and reachable only by id, so it can be obtained and still not be mirrorable because the manifest is generated and never hand-edited. Both --adopt and --selftest return before the Google modules load, structurally, so neither needs a token.

nodes.label: ok-adopted, never ok
nodes.rationale: The download path verifies byte count and Drive's own md5Checksum; an adopted file has had only the byte count checked, and writing ok would claim a verification never performed.

nodes.label: The by-id route is a verification route, not a fetch route
nodes.rationale: get_file_metadata on a bare id returns a duplicate title and needs no token, moving the duplicate claim from stated to corroborated; the connector returns no md5Checksum, so a file can share a size and an opening and still differ in the middle.

nodes.label: The Colab mount is the route
nodes.rationale: There is deliberately no Google token: drive_sync.py's OAuth flow ends at run_local_server, which a headless container cannot serve, and --token would mean transporting a refresh token into a session.

nodes.label: PENDING.tsv is maintained beside the mirror, not generated
nodes.rationale: A correction to an earlier note: the string pending does not occur in drive_sync.py, which is why --adopt reads it and leaves it alone.

nodes.label: The __<fileId> duplicate-title rule
nodes.rationale: Drive lets several files in one folder share a title and a filesystem does not; the most recently modified copy keeps the plain name, ties broken by ascending id so the assignment is stable across runs.

nodes.label: Google-native docs are exports, not byte-exact copies
nodes.rationale: Docs to Markdown, Sheets to CSV, Slides to PDF, Drawings to PNG; the recorded size is the export's, formatting is lost, and Drive refuses to export a native document over 10 MB.

nodes.label: --folder replaces the folder list and narrows the manifest
nodes.rationale: The manifest is regenerated from what a run walked, so syncing one folder alone drops the other folder's rows; --only is the safe way to do less work.

nodes.label: No line-ending translation under drive/
nodes.rationale: Six mirrored files genuinely contain CRLF, and rewriting line endings on checkout would silently invalidate the md5s recorded in MANIFEST.tsv.

nodes.label: The two 370 MiB chat exports
nodes.rationale: Both titled conversations.json and both exactly 388,264,753 bytes, 3.7x GitHub's hard per-file limit; every route produces the same file, so this is not a transfer problem and no transfer method solves it.

nodes.label: Splitting the export into 90M parts is the wrong answer
nodes.rationale: Arbitrary byte ranges of dense JSON do not delta-compress and the parts are inert — nothing can read, diff, grep or index them — so you pay git's price for none of git's benefits.

nodes.label: shard_conversations.py — one readable JSON per conversation
nodes.rationale: The only option that makes the content searchable in the repo and indexable by Graphify; ijson keeps a 370 MiB input at flat memory, and the script re-reads and re-parses every shard it wrote before reporting success.
